text: dsh-tarot 是一个面向 DSH Web 客户端的三张塔罗牌抽取插件。它注册 tarot_draw 工具，并在对话区提供 78 张暗牌的选牌界面，让用户依次选择过去、现在和未来对应的三张不同牌；随后显示牌名、正逆位、图片与来源链接，并把来源页提取的牌义要点交给模型参考。适合希望在 DSH 对话中进行三牌阵占卜、查看牌面来源并结合实际情况继续讨论的用户。运行时需要联网访问 w.taluo.com 获取抽中牌的图片和解释内容，不需要额外 API key。

dsh-tarot adds tarot_draw to DSH Web chat. Users choose three face-down cards for past, present, and future. Results show names, orientations, images, and links; selected-page notes go to the model. Meanings and images load from w.taluo.com, requiring network access. No extra API key is needed.
想在 DSH 里抽三张牌看看过去、现在和未来。
能不能让我自己从牌背里选牌，再看每张牌的正逆位和牌义来源？
I want a three-card tarot reading in my DSH chat, with source-linked meanings for the cards I choose.
dsh-tarot 的功能「三张牌抽取」：模型调用 tarot_draw 后，用户在对话中的 78 张牌背网格里依次选三张，分别对应过去、现在和未来；插件揭示牌名与正逆位，并返回牌阵结果。
dsh-tarot 的功能「牌面来源展示」：抽牌完成后，插件获取三张牌对应的解释页面并提取有限长度的要点；结果行展示牌图和来源链接，来源不可用时会保留抽牌结果并标记说明不可用。
dsh-tarot 使用前须知：抽牌后会请求 w.taluo.com 上所选牌的解释页，网页也从该站加载牌图，需联网。（见 src/source.ts:66-75；src/client/index.tsx:132-136）

dsh-tarot README · Summary：Draw three distinct cards from a 78-card Rider–Waite–Smith deck, ordered as past influences, present situation, and future direction. The Web page spreads all 78 face-down cards across the conversation width without an inner scrollbar. Each draw reshuffles card identities, and each click removes one chosen back. The result includes images and interpretation notes fetched from the selected upright or reversed pages on [w.taluo.com](https://w.taluo.com/index.html). The model can explain the spread, ask about your circumstances, and refine its reading using the same cards.

dsh-tarot README · Table of Contents：- [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note)

dsh-tarot README · Use this package：The tested runtime is DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` with Cordis `4.0.5` and Node `^22.19.0 || >=24`. Install the prebuilt GitHub Release into your existing Web profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/auwc/dsh-tarot/releases/download/v0.5.0/dsh-tarot-0.5.0.tgz
dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

dsh-tarot README · Use this package：The composed configuration contains a `tarot` row. Start your Web profile normally and ask “Draw three tarot cards for my current situation.” The model calls `tarot_draw({ question: "My current situation" })` and waits for your three clicks. The result then shows the selected cards, positions, orientations, image links, and source pages. Model access still uses your profile's configured provider. The close button shows “Hide card choices” or “Cancel draw” according to the question type; hiding the panel leaves the tool request pending.

dsh-tarot README · Use this package：The bundle supplies these configuration fields. When replacing the `tarot` row's configuration, provide all three fields:

| Field | Bundle value | Accepted values |
|---|---|---|
| `reversedPermille` | `500` | Integer 0–1000; 0 gives all upright, 1000 all reversed |
| `maxQuestionChars` | `500` | Integer 1–10000; trimmed Unicode code points |
| `sourceTimeoutMs` | `5000` | Integer 100–30000; maximum wait per selected source page |
dsh-tarot README · Use this package：Blank questions and questions exceeding the configured limit fail before drawing. Card count and positions are fixed; extra input fields cannot change them.

dsh-tarot README · Understand the implementation：The named Cordis plugin registers a tool whose disposer belongs to its plugin scope. Node's `crypto.randomInt` shuffles all 78 card identities before displaying their hidden positions. The tool waits on `userQuestions.ask` for three distinct positions selected in order by the user. Orientations use separate random draws after the answer. The tool fetches only the three revealed interpretation pages, extracts bounded notes, and records them with the selected cards in the tool result. Native tool results retain readable text and `meta.tarot`, so saved results do not depend on drawing again. `scripts/crawl-catalog.mjs` refreshes the 78-card link catalog from the site's five index pages; it does not bundle images or article text.

dsh-tarot README · Understand the implementation：From the independent package directory, install locked dependencies and run the checks:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm pack

dsh-tarot README · Understand the implementation：Tests cover the deck, deterministic edge choices, input validation, cancellation, disposal, and a real Loader/agent-loop composition with a scripted model. Two recorded sessions replay upright and reversed draws without an API key. Only the composition test's random source is mocked; published DSH runtime packages execute normally.

dsh-tarot README · Model Experience：The profile gains one tool schema and a consultation instruction. Each successful native call adds the question, three card names/positions/orientations, source URLs, and extracted notes to model context; the deck's other cards do not enter the prompt. The model is instructed to give a provisional reading, check a specific card-based hypothesis against the user's experience, then ask what happened and what makes the situation difficult as needed. It asks one main question at a time and revises the same spread after each answer. The note fields are source material, not a deterministic interpretation; model wording and question choice vary. Ordinary model caching applies.

dsh-tarot README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：Card images and interpretation notes load from the source site, so they require network access and may change there. No image or article is bundled. If a page fails, the result marks its notes unavailable; the model is instructed not to attribute its own reading to that page. Headless runs without a user-question answerer cannot draw. Reusing cards for follow-up questions is a model instruction, not an enforced deduplication rule; a new tool invocation draws again. A crash before the result is logged has no recoverable selection. Nested PTC calls return JSON but do not persist the dedicated presentation metadata; the outer program must return the facts it needs to retain.
